request.label: How e-Move plans a trip
request.hint: Scroll to plan an electric car trip with e-Move, from the battery to the charging station.

stops.name: Range
stops.title: How far the car goes
stops.text: It all starts in the garage. VeiculoService rejects battery levels outside 0 to 100 and works out the range: a Tesla Model 3 does 491 km on a full battery; at 80%, 392.8 km are left.

stops.name: Addresses
stops.title: Addresses become coordinates
stops.text: Origin and destination come in as text. GeocodingService asks LocationIQ where they are and returns the latitude and longitude for the pins on the map.

stops.name: Route
stops.title: How far it can go
stops.text: The route comes from LocationIQ through /api/directions. e-Move keeps 20% of the battery as a reserve: at 80%, the safe range is 294.6 km. This trip is 512 km, so the car has to stop before the marked point.

stops.name: Stations
stops.title: Where to charge
stops.text: Near the point where the reserve starts, OpenChargeMap is searched within 93 km. The first station joins the route, the battery goes back to 90%, and the math repeats until the destination is within range.

stops.name: Trip
stops.title: Trip saved
stops.text: With one charge, that's 512 km and 61.4 kg of CO₂ saved. POST /api/viagens reads the user from the JWT and saves the trip to MariaDB in one transaction. Further down, you can try the range math with another car.
